name: 1630 Prairie Avenue — small earlier frame house, K16 clapboard

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The register's 'Civil War era' is a chronology no source here states for 1630, so no building date is claimed.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 34.000, v -1.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.58 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1630 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1630 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle inside the traced main part of s20fp-1630-b1 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), kept from the draft (13.25 m deep, 5.5 m along the front). The wing on its south side at the rear and the porch across the front are frame_house blocks (form.frame_house), also kept from the draft's fit.

stories.note: '2BB' printed on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys. The 'BB' is not read as two basements (the register's guard); the house stands on a low foundation over an unstated cellar.

construction.note: Drawn yellow, the sheet's colour for frame. Built board by board from the K16 timber kit at a frame wall's 0.15 m, never with a masonry wall's thickness or a stone texture.

frame_house.note: The whole house from the K16 kit (T-2357). READ from the sheet through the T-2328 trace s20fp-1630-b1 and the draft's fit of it: the main block's rectangle (13.25 m deep, 5.5 m along Prairie, the footprint below), the two-storey wing on its south side at the rear (u 1.0-4.5, 2.25 m out, the draft's r2) and the one-storey frame piece across the front (the porch, 1.5 m deep, the draft's r3). Everything else is RECONSTRUCTED from the kit and recorded as L-k16-1630-frame-house-2357: clapboard on a water table over a 0.45 m foundation, corner boards, two-over-two sash in flat timber casings (three bays on the front, three a storey on each long side, two on the rear), a four-panel door at the north end of the front, a deep frieze under a boxed eave with scroll brackets round both blocks, the low 22-degree hip on the main block and a flat deck on the lower wing, one brick stack on the ridge, the kit porch across the front with timber steps to the door, and a fawn body paint.

roof_covering.note: No roof covering has been read for 1630. A Civil War era frame house of this size was commonly shingled, and the weathered grey-brown of cedar is RECONSTRUCTED, the colour 1638's K16 front uses; the shingles themselves are not modelled. The wing's flat deck takes the same colour.

boundary.note: T-3230 (piece 2 of T-3216; the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door and its front boundaries, and where no picture shows them a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of this front is held. Every pictured west front of the 1600 block closes its street line and opens it only at the walk: 1612's photograph (an iron spear fence), 1620's 1874 engraving and 1898 sketch (iron lattice), 1616's 1874 view (boards), and 1638's photograph, the block's other timber house (iron bars on a pale stone base, 0.32 m, the bars to 0.83 m, an open gateway between two piers with no leaf in it); the seven unpictured K01 houses of the west side were closed on that reading (T-3229). So this front is closed the way the K16 kit closes a frame house's (archetypes/k16_yard.py, as 1720's): a squared stone kerb 0.35 m through on the street line, its top 0.32 m up, with an iron railing on it to 0.83 m (1638's base and bar heights), from the south lot line to the north, and an opening 1.5 m clear on the porch stair's axis (s 4.35) between two stone posts 0.35 m square and 1.2 m high (1720's posts), with no leaf in it, as at 1638. The street line and lot lines are parcel prairie_1630's (data/street_grid/1904.json, read off the 1911 sheet) carried into the house's plan frame by the placement its sidecar holds (the transform that puts 1720's recorded street line, u 31.2, back on its parcel to the centimetre): the street line u 21.36-21.37, the lot lines s -2.535 and 6.035, the lines 1634's and 1628's fronts meet. RECONSTRUCTED: the kind of boundary, its heights and materials, the posts and the opening's width and place (liberty L-k16-walks-1600-block-3230).

yard.note: T-3230. A front walk in flags straight out from the porch stair's foot (read off the built steps) through the kerb's opening between the posts to the street line, the public walk's inner edge, 1.2 m wide in 0.9 m flags 0.06 m over the ground, the district's K14 walk sizes. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, width and surface; no picture shows them (liberty L-k16-walks-1600-block-3230). No lawn is laid: the yard's ground is the app's own (generators/archetypes/k16_yard.py).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2BB frame (yellow) dwelling (D) with a 1-storey frame piece at its Prairie face'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2357 (piece 3 of T-1862) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the whole house is rebuilt from the K16 timber kit — clapboard walls built board by board on a water table, cased two-over-two sash and a panelled door, a bracketed boxed eave, a low hip with one brick stack, the kit porch across the front with its steps — instead of the draft builder. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '2BB', frame, the traced main body, the rear wing on the south and the one-storey piece across the front) through the T-1840 census and the T-2328 trace. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k16-1630-frame-house-2357. No photograph, plate or description of 1630 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
